# code-standards

One deterministic quality gate for Sarj Python, TypeScript, Swift, Kotlin, shell, SQL, IaC, and repository policy.

```bash
uv tool install --python 3.15 code-standards
```

Adopt the repository once with `code-standards setup`. It installs one canonical staged gate that includes semantic lint and repository policy, plus commit-message and pull-request history enforcement. Do not install Repo Standards separately.

The pre-commit gate runs once on every commit and discovers paths directly from the Git index, including mixed file types and deletion-only commits. The shared dispatcher selects applicable rules and retains type analysis, repository policy, exclusions and suppression accountability. Errors and incomplete analysis block the commit; warning-stage findings stay visible even when the hook passes. Generated hooks apply safe custom-rule, Ruff and ESLint fixes automatically. When a fix changes a staged file, the gate stops so you can review and stage the edit, then retry. Use `code-standards fix --staged` to apply fixes separately, or `check --fix` to fix before checking. Staged fixes never fall back to the whole repository and refuse files with unstaged changes.

Setup installs the selected hook manager. In a fresh checkout, run `code-standards doctor --repair` before committing; doctor checks installation and the exact unconditional command. Conditional Lefthook jobs must be moved to an unconditional job without changing unrelated hooks. Git can bypass local hooks with `--no-verify`; the canonical CI gate independently enforces policy.

```bash
code-standards setup
code-standards check
code-standards check --rule python:no-excessive-cognitive-complexity src/
code-standards fix
code-standards doctor
code-standards update
```

New ESLint setups use `eslint.config.ts` and the compiler-checked `eslint.strict.ts` preset. Existing `.mjs` preset imports remain supported; to migrate, remove the old generated preset and change its imports to `.ts` before running setup.

Use repeatable `check --rule ENGINE:ID` selectors to select native rules, ESLint rules, or managed security audits. Exclusions, baselines, and severities still apply; Ruff selectors are not supported. Native linters and ESLint execute only selected rules. ESLint retains configured parsers, options, severities, and suppression directives.

For a history-free initial import, set `SARJ_STANDARDS_INITIAL_IMPORT_SOURCE` only on the initial commit process to the full lowercase object ID of an available source commit with exactly one available parent. HEAD must be an unborn branch; the entire staged tree must equal that commit, tracked worktree files must match the index without hidden index flags, and nonignored files must be staged. Native staged checks compare the source commit with its parent, preserving the usual changed-line failures for findings introduced in that commit while allowing inherited diagnostic budgets. Validation runs before and after analysis; all analyzers and baseline limits still apply. The caller must qualify the source commit separately. Git replacement objects and lazy fetching are disabled; explicitly supplied temporary object alternates may provide the source history without copying it into the new repository. Remove the input and alternates before subsequent commits, pushes, and CI. Invalid or changed import context fails analysis, including clean reports; ordinary checks without this input retain their existing behavior.

Selected ESLint checks apply live inline suppressions and validate selected bulk suppression counts. The complete lint gate owns unused inline-directive and inline-configuration checks: a partial run cannot establish whether an unselected rule's directive is needed.

The complete Python and JavaScript/TypeScript source gate requires named, line-local exceptions with concrete reasons. SARJ523 rejects blanket Python waivers, scoped Ruff file/range disables and weakened Pyright source settings; SARJ419 also rejects missing explanations. Bare sarj-noqa markers cannot waive Python, SQL or IaC findings. Required Ruff blanket-ignore checks and an independent ESLint suppression-policy pass remain active despite source disables, consumer rule configuration, rule exclusions and diagnostic baselines. The ESLint pass bans file/range disables, ts-ignore and ts-nocheck while retaining described local ts-expect-error exceptions. Generated-source headers cannot authorize their own waiver; explicit whole-path exclusions retain that boundary. A reason is not proof that an exception is justified. Native parse/read/size failures make checks incomplete. Explicit tool delegation, partial and own-CI options retain their declared scope and coverage notices.

The complete Standards gate enforces Ruff's ban on `typing.cast` and `typing_extensions.cast` even when source comments, consumer Ruff configuration or manifest rule exceptions suppress `banned-api`; these cast findings cannot enter or consume the diagnostic baseline. Wildcard imports, bounded literal `getattr` names and proven read-only typing module namespace lookups through `__dict__`, `vars` and `__getattribute__` retain the same ban. Other banned APIs retain their existing exception policy. Prefer discriminated unions, explicit narrowing and typed contracts. The warning `python:no-dual-shape-model-field-reader` (SARJ522) identifies private helpers that read the same declared Pydantic fields through model `getattr` and mapping lookup branches, returning `object` or `Any`. Normalize raw input once and read typed attributes. Opaque inputs, raw validators and genuinely dynamic reflection remain supported. Review changes to missing-field handling, coercion, generated defaults and validation errors; there is no autofix.

Python boolean traps are owned by Ruff FBT001, FBT002 and FBT003: positional boolean annotations, defaults and literal arguments are checked; keyword-only inputs, named arguments and the existing test exemptions remain allowed. The typed ESLint policy uses `@sarj/no-boolean-selector-parameter` at warning severity. Its owned detector checks single-statement operation selectors and concise-arrow conditional dispatch. Prefer separate intention-revealing operations or an explicit string-literal mode. Boolean data, syntactic value mappings, stable same-operation data choices, setters and independently declared callback or inherited contracts remain allowed. Independent JSX helpers are checked; types and references establish callback contracts. It requires type information and a direct broad-boolean parameter condition. Multi-statement bodies, short-circuit guards, nullable or literal-only inputs and indirect predicates remain outside its scope. The preserved block-body `onX` property exemption remains a documented blind spot. Use `code-standards check --rule eslint:no-boolean-selector-parameter` to inspect it. Noncomputed property reads count as data without proving getter effects; computed reads, including literal keys, remain outside that exemption. API changes require manual review; the rule provides no automatic rewrite.

The shared ESLint policy also warns on unparenthesized assignments in returned expressions through native `no-return-assign`. Review whether the assignment should be a comparison or a separate state change; there is no automatic intent-changing fix. The native `except-parens` option accepts individually grouped assignments and common lazy memoization. Parentheses mark syntactic visibility, not proven intent: formatters can add or remove them without changing behavior. A chained assignment can still warn after formatting even when its outer expression is grouped. For an intentional local-variable chain, use separate assignment statements followed by return. Upstream may report several writes at the same return location. This rule does not prohibit all returned mutations or prove command/query separation. Existing typed void-return and Promise checks retain their own boundaries; an executor's returned expression alone does not prove a broken Promise.

Native ESLint warnings also cover ignored Promise executor return values, unchanged loop conditions, interpolation placeholders in ordinary quoted strings and self-comparisons. A returned executor expression may deliberately discard a value, identical-looking calls can have different effects, and literal interpolation text can be an external template contract. Regex assertion contradictions and redundant assertions are warnings requiring review of matching and capture behavior; backtracking and disjunction checks remain deferred. These controls do not apply automatic intent-changing rewrites.

The shared source policy bans JavaScript for-in loops through the native ForInStatement selector, which replaces the narrower typed array-loop diagnostic. Prefer for-of over Object.keys or Object.entries for own properties; inherited enumeration contracts require an exact explained exception. Native no-restricted-properties, no-proto and no-iterator reject legacy arguments.callee/caller, __proto__ member access and __iterator__ member access. The arguments restriction covers dot access, static bracket access and destructuring without duplicate no-caller diagnostics. Object-literal prototype declarations and data strings remain distinct. Existing no-eval rejects direct and indirect JavaScript eval. Python eval and breakpoint calls retain Ruff S307 and T100 as their native owners, including the configured preview eval-reference checks.

The shared ESLint policy includes `@shadcn/lint` design-system guidance at warning severity. It runs where upstream discovery finds `components.json` or a Tailwind theme, or where the consumer explicitly declares `settings.shadcn.ui` or `componentImports`. Ordinary CSS projects receive no Tailwind-specific findings. Component layout classes and arbitrary layout measurements remain allowed; appearance overrides and off-token appearance values receive guidance. Discovered component implementation files are exempt from restyling, arbitrary-value and static-class checks, while inline-style and unknown-class checks remain active. Raw colors remain owned by `@sarj/prefer-semantic-colors`.

Use `code-standards check --rule eslint:shadcn/no-restyle` to inspect one upstream rule. Declare shared-package imports and custom class helpers in `settings.shadcn`, scoped to each application's files in the consumer's ESLint configuration. Add reviewed component contracts or exact class/property allowances through the upstream rule options; do not replace every warning with a global error. Tailwind theme-loading warnings indicate grammar fallback with reduced coverage. The project-discovery API is experimental and is protected by an exact dependency pin and executable integration tests.

Terraform, Kubernetes, and GitHub Actions adoption adds isolated Checkov 3.3.30 and zizmor 1.31.1 runtimes. Setup and generated CI prewarm these tools; checks run offline with packaged policy. Use `--rule checkov:CKV_GCP_95` or `--rule zizmor:template-injection` to select upstream audits. Their findings start as warnings, use the canonical diagnostic baseline, and retain upstream IDs. Checkov honors its inline suppression directives; zizmor ignore comments are disabled. Explicit zizmor selectors include auditor-persona checks; online-only audits cannot run offline. Parsing or execution failures leave the analysis incomplete. Image digest evidence for source templates is deferred to their rendered deployment artifacts.

The opt-in `jscpd` capability runs the jscpd 5.4.0 copy-paste detector, which setup installs through mise. Setup and upgrades list it in `[capabilities].disable`; remove it there to enable it. Each check scans Python, TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin source outside test directories, because a copy can only be found by comparing it with the whole tree. Every repeated block of at least 50 tokens is a `jscpd:duplicate-code` warning on its own lines that names the other copies, so the changed-line baseline reports it when either side is edited. The repository's own jscpd configuration is ignored.

The `shfmt` capability checks shell files, including extensionless shebang entrypoints, with shfmt 3.14.1 using two-space indentation and indented case clauses. Explicit, staged and PR-selected files must be formatted in full; full scans report existing drift as warnings. Formatting errors on selected files cannot be hidden by a diagnostic baseline. `code-standards fix` formats selected files safely, preserving executable permissions; generated Gradle launchers are excluded. Shebangs determine the shell before filename suffixes, including supported shells at custom absolute paths. Bats files use the upstream Bats formatter dialect. Zsh formatting does not provide ShellCheck coverage: its unsupported dialect remains an explicit coverage failure. Ambient editor settings cannot change the canonical style, and simplification is disabled.

Shell libraries with a shell suffix or no suffix can declare their dialect with a top-level `# shellcheck shell=bash` header before executable source. Quoted dialect values and preceding directive fields are supported. An executable shebang remains authoritative. Generated Gradle exclusions require the exact generator comment in the source header; mentions in strings, heredocs and ordinary prose do not exempt authored scripts. Automatic fixes refuse native formatter output that removes carriage-return bytes, so literal data and line endings need manual review in those cases.

ShellCheck and shfmt also inspect executable shell fields in workflows, composite actions, Cloud Build, Make and Mise using the same policy as shell files. Analysis follows the configured interpreter, including inherited Actions shells and Cloud Build shebangs, and reports positions in the authored configuration. Actions expressions are masked for native parsing with their quoted string boundaries preserved, and actionlint retains workflow validation while shared ShellCheck supplies shell findings once. Docker shell semantics remain owned by Hadolint. Fixes can format verified literal YAML blocks while preserving scalar headers, newlines and decoded execution source. Folded scalars, aliases, templates, argv, Make and Mise remain check-only; extract complex programs to shell files for independently linted execution.

The shared argv parser records effective `errexit` and `pipefail` options in order, including later `+e` and `+o` disables. Interpreter option operands and arguments after the script or command payload do not activate runtime checks.

The shared ShellCheck policy enables `check-set-e-suppressed` alongside the existing `check-extra-masked-returns`. SC2310 and SC2311 warn when function calls suppress `set -e`, including conditional calls and command substitutions. Review intentional predicates and use justified native ShellCheck suppressions where appropriate; these findings have no automatic semantic fix. SC2312 remains enabled to detect masked exit status. The repository shell gate prints the new warnings without failing for them and retains its existing blocking checks. The managed `.shellcheckrc` retains the existing native gate checks; Standards enables these advisory checks explicitly because direct ShellCheck exits nonzero for informational findings.

For concise Bash, preserve arguments with quoted expansions and command arrays, use a literal `printf` format, and handle fallible commands explicitly. Built-in lookup and parameter expansion can replace external commands when their lookup, output and exit-status contracts agree. These choices use existing upstream checks; intentional stream contracts and predicates require review rather than automatic semantic rewrites.

The opt-in `knip` capability uses Knip 6.42.1 production mode. Remove it from `[capabilities].disable` and declare `application = true` under `[knip]` to enable advisory `knip:files` evidence. Version one supports a single private application with entry and project arrays containing production patterns ending in `!` in `knip.json` or `.knip.json`. Native aliases and framework entries remain authoritative; unresolved imports, configuration diagnostics, workspaces and dynamic configuration make the graph inconclusive. Review runtime and public owners before deleting a module. No automatic fixes or application inference are performed.

Unused private Python test helpers require `reportUnusedFunction` set to `warning` in the consumer's existing BasedPyright test execution environments. This bundle preserves native configuration and bounds test warnings to authored, undecorated module-level private helpers in conventional test paths. Decorated fixtures, methods and production callbacks are excluded; no consumer diagnostic setting is enabled automatically. Existing production diagnostics are preserved.

`check --jobs 2` overlaps native analysis with the external-tool pipeline. The default is `--jobs 1`; external tools remain sequential and report ordering is deterministic.

Public Python suggested edits retain `expected_source_hash`, the lowercase SHA-256 digest of the exact captured source bytes, alongside `expected_text_hash` for the replaced slice. Use `to_json(report, include_fix_source_hashes=True)` or the same keyword on report, diagnostic, fix or edit `as_dict` to emit `expectedSourceHash`. The default JSON output is unchanged. Opted-in JSON requires the updated bundled `analysis.schema.json`; older strict v1 schemas reject the added field. This provenance does not apply edits or validate a current file, and SARIF output is unchanged.

DevOps execution blocks may sequence existing commands without helper scripts. Keep interpreter source, control flow, logical chains, pipelines and substitutions in independently linted files; Python `-m` and script paths, and jq/awk `-f` files remain supported. SARJ310 is an error, including short inline programs. Cloud Build SARJ315 checks YAML and JSON for unique IDs, ordered step dependencies, script/argv exclusivity and untrusted substitutions in shell source; pass substitutions as quoted arguments to external scripts. JSON configs are discovered in operational directories or with `cloudbuild` in their filename; JSON syntax must be strict, with unique keys and finite numbers. Files named with `cloudbuild`, and Build-shaped files under a `cloudbuild` directory, use the bundled, digest-verified Google Build v1 field schema for field names, types, enums and protobuf durations/integers. The offline schema rejects output-only fields; trigger expansion, resource access and hosted admission require the deployment environment.

The source gate uses pinned actionlint, shared ShellCheck, offline Zizmor, Hadolint and Skaffold v4beta7 schema validation. Every selected `action.yml`/`action.yaml` uses GitHub's pinned action parser and converter offline, including composite steps, expression syntax and available contexts, runtime requirements, step IDs and action-reference forms. This uses the core Node runtime and needs no referencing workflow, consumer npm setup or security capability. Cloud Deploy validation is a documented partial structural contract. Terraform validation and TFLint require explicit repository trust and prepared local providers; analysis never initializes or downloads them. Compose requires an exact consumer `[devops].compose_version`; its source check does not resolve environment inputs. Declare `compose_projects = [["base.yaml", "overlays/production.yaml"]]` in `[devops]` to validate custom filenames and overlays in invocation order. Selecting any member checks the whole project; declared fragments are not checked independently. Undeclared conventional filenames remain standalone projects. Missing inputs and native field errors fail coverage. Source checks use Compose's partially resolved model; full consistency requires the actual deployment environment.

File discovery, enabled capabilities and native validation each determine coverage. Check the selected paths and tool reports; a syntax check does not establish deployment validity.

| Format | Specialized coverage | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Terraform `.tf`, `.tf.json` | Native validation, TFLint and applicable Sarj rules | Local providers and explicit trust required; JSON is never passed to `fmt` |
| `.tfvars`, `.tftest.hcl` | Native Terraform formatting | Variable/test files do not select module validation or TFLint |
| `.tfvars.json`, `.tftest.json`, other `.hcl` | Applicable Sarj rules | No native formatting; JSON semantic coverage is limited |
| Actions workflows and action metadata | actionlint for workflows; pinned GitHub action parser for all `action.yml`/`action.yaml` files, including composite steps; Zizmor and shared execution checks | Offline validation covers structure and expression syntax/contexts; expression values and runtime availability require GitHub; security capabilities may be disabled |
| Cloud Build YAML/JSON | Pinned Google Build v1 field schema, SARJ315 and shared execution checks | Schema selection uses a `cloudbuild` filename or Build-shaped source in that directory; trigger inputs and hosted admission remain external |
| Dockerfile variants | Hadolint and executable-field checks | Image-default entrypoints are not inferred |
| Conventional Compose filenames and declared `compose_projects` | Pinned native Compose validation of ordered file groups | Environment interpolation/resolution stays disabled; deployment must supply its actual environment inputs |
| Skaffold and Cloud Deploy YAML | Pinned Skaffold schema; partial Cloud Deploy structure | Generated resources need prepared validation |
| Helm charts, Kubernetes and CRDs | Prepared Helm lint/render, kubeconform and kube-linter | Receipts must bind the rendered artifacts and local schema closure |
| Templates, systemd units, Nginx, Kamailio, Prometheus and Compose configs | Prepared native validation of rendered files with the matching runtime | Declare prepared targets and hash their authored inputs, rendered files and include closure; other service formats need their own application validator |

Native prepared targets use `kind` values `systemd`, `nginx`, `kamailio`, `prometheus-config`, `prometheus-rules` or `compose`, plus `native_version`, `manifests` and `artifacts`. `native_version` is the exact first version-output line of the installed validator; Nginx writes it to stderr. Compose instead uses its exact semantic version and requires a hashed `environment_file`; ordered `manifests` run through native `config --quiet` with full interpolation and consistency checks. List executable artifacts under `executables` when unit validation requires them. Render templates first and bind template/variable inputs with `source_inputs`. The gate verifies hashes, stages a private copy and invokes only the service's check mode. Native service validation requires explicit repository trust and the deployment's matching runtime, including any referenced modules or runtime files; it never installs or starts a service. Systemd disables generators and verifies against the staged root. Other validators may resolve absolute runtime paths on the validation host; this is not a filesystem sandbox.

Release gates use `code-standards analyze --prepared-only --prepared-devops prepared.json --prepared-target TARGET_ID`; add `--trust-repository-code` for native service and Compose targets. Declare exact `prepared_targets` under `[devops]` with an authored `source` path. Version-one receipts bind target IDs, authored input hashes, staged chart archives, ordered values, typed set arguments, manifests and a hashed local schema closure. Helm 4.3.1 strict lint and stage-specific rendering feed kubeconform 0.8.0 and kube-linter 0.8.3. Missing tools, schemas, targets and invalid receipts fail the gate. Prepared-only findings bypass source debt baselines; container exceptions require exact target, GVK, namespace, object, check, container kind, container name and a reason, and stale exceptions fail.

Prepared YAML rejects duplicate parsed keys and cyclic aliases. Each document must stay below depth 64 and at or below 100,000 expanded nodes, including repeated aliases.

Source-only checks report prepared validation as deferred. They do not certify generated manifests or replace Cloud Deploy, Cloud Build or Kubernetes admission validation. Run `setup --tools-only` in CI after installing the bundle and the pinned mise bootstrap. It requires an existing manifest, installs and attests the applicable native tools, and preserves repository wiring. Release analysis consumes prepared bytes without pulling charts.
